question: The final European medal count at the Olympic Games was 309. To highlight this sporting excellence by the nations of the Old Continent, the Commission launched a European medal counter. This excellent, unprecedented and symbolic initiative seeks to showcase the values of the European Union and of the Olympic movement, as enshrined in the motto ‘United in Diversity’.

It should be noted too that for the first time at the 2024 Paris Olympics the 12 gold stars of the European flag hung, and will continue to hang, alongside the French and Olympic flags at the competition sites of the Olympic and Paralympic Games.

In line with these very good initiatives, would the Commission agree to ask the Olympic Committee to display a European flag as an inlaid image behind the national flag of an EU Member State for European athletes and delegations?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.10.2024) The Commission deeply supports the autonomy of sport and hence respects the decision of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to use the flag, the emblem and the anthem adopted by the National Olympic Committees and approved by the IOC Executive Board. It therefore acknowledges that no exceptions to this rule are currently allowed.

Notwithstanding, the Commission welcomes the strong European dimension of the Paris 2024 Olympic Games and the fact that for the first time the EU flag was prominently displayed in venues alongside the Olympic flag. It considers that its partnership with the Paris 2024 Olympic Games provided a unique opportunity for the EU to promote its core values such as unity and diversity, including through the medal counter.
The Commission will continue to support EU visibility at such significant sporting events in the future.
